name: Παραλία Αγ. Σπυρίδωνα Λουτρακίου
evidence: No source found for this specific beach; all 'Agios Spyridonas' results refer to Corfu/Leros and 'Loutraki' results to Korinthia/Crete.

name: Παραλία Διόνι
evidence: Dioni (Katochi, Acheloos delta) described as wild natural beauty with a traditional food/drink establishment; no mention of sunbeds or beach bar.

name: Παραλία Λουτρακίου
evidence: Only beachsearcher (auto-generated) lists sunbeds/cafes for a 'Loutraki Beach, West Greece'; no reliable source clearly matching this Amvrakikos-area beach.

name: Παραλία Πλατανίτη
evidence: Nafpaktia municipality/local guides describe Platanitis (4 km from the Rio-Antirrio bridge) as organized with restaurants, cafes and sunbeds.

name: ΠΔΕ Πάτρα Αγ.Βασίλειος
evidence: Agios Vasileios (Rio, Patras) described as largely organized with umbrellas and loungers, beach bars along the coast, plus a Seatrac access ramp.

name: Ματζάκουρα
evidence: Described as not organized with no loungers for rent (camping a few meters behind), near Katakolo/Agios Andreas.

name: Παραλία Λεβεντοχωρίου
evidence: Pyrgos hoteliers/Visit Olympia listings: beach has umbrellas, loungers, WC, showers and a canteen with tables serving swimmers.

name: Παραλία Πατητηρίου
evidence: Patitiri port has a small beach with clear waters; sources mention no sunbeds/umbrellas there (nearest organized beach is Rousoum Gialos).

name: Άγιος Πέτρος
evidence: Explicitly described as a non-organized pebble beach in a bay, one of the island's most secluded.

name: Γλυφά
evidence: Glyfa (Alonissos) has fine white pebble and umbrellas with sunbeds at its southern end.

name: Παραλία Βότση
evidence: Votsi cove described as organized with umbrellas and sunbeds; tavernas in the small harbor village.

name: Παραλία Μεγάλος Μουρτιάς
evidence: Megalos Mourtias has umbrellas, sunbeds and a cafeteria under the olive trees.

name: Πλάκες
evidence: Rock-slab swimming spot near Patitiri; no source found describing any facilities.

name: Ρουσούμ Γιαλός
evidence: Rousoum Gialos is small but organized with umbrellas and sunbeds, plus 3-4 tavernas and cafes on the beach.

name: Τζώρτζη
evidence: Tzortzi Gialos only described scenically (emerald waters, pine forest); no explicit sunbed/bar evidence found for this beach itself.

name: Τσουκαλιά
evidence: Tsoukalia (largest north-side beach) has a few sunbeds and umbrellas plus a canteen for essentials.

name: Παραλία Κάστρου
evidence: Sources conflict: one says only a canteen and no umbrellas/sunbeds, another says the canteen offers umbrellas and sunbeds; canteen presence is consistent.

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης
evidence: Agios Ioannis sto Kastri (Mamma Mia chapel beach) has umbrellas/sunbeds (very few for the crowds) and a canteen serving coffee, drinks and cold food.

name: Έλιος
evidence: Elios beach (Neo Klima) is organized with umbrellas and sunbeds managed by the adjacent cafeteria; canoe rental available.

name: Χόβολο
evidence: Hovolo is explicitly described as a hidden, unorganized beach (in contrast to neighboring Elios).

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης
evidence: Agios Ioannis (East Pelion) is fully organized, Blue Flag, with sunbeds, umbrellas, showers, beach bar, lifeguard and water sports.

name: Βρωμονέρι
evidence: Only hiking-trail references found for Pelion's Vromoneri (Katigiorgis trail); detailed facility descriptions found belong to the Messinia beach of the same name.

name: Καλλιφτέρη
evidence: Kallifteri (Afissos) is organized with 3 beach bars, sunbeds and umbrellas, showers, lifeguard and water sports.

name: Καστρί
evidence: Kastri (South Pelion) has a small organized section with umbrellas in front of Kastri Beach Camping, which runs a cafe bar and restaurant; plenty of free space too.

name: Μικρό
evidence: Mikro described as picturesque and calm next to Platanias; the explicit beach-bar-with-sunbeds mention refers to Platanias beach, not Mikro itself.

name: Μορτίτσα
evidence: Described only as a solitary beach just after Mourtias for people who want to be alone; no facility info.

name: Μουρτιάς
evidence: Mourtias (Promyri, South Pelion) is explicitly completely unorganized — no shop for water/food, bring your own umbrella.

name: Νταμούχαρη
evidence: Damouchari described as a picturesque natural harbor with big white pebbles and tavernas; no explicit mention of sunbeds/umbrellas on the beach.

name: Πάλτση
evidence: Paltsi described as an alternative beach near Argalasti with minimal accommodation; no explicit sunbed/bar evidence either way.

name: Παραλία Ανάληψης
evidence: Name collision: the well-documented Analipsi near Pouri is wild with no tourist amenities or loungers, but an Analipsi also exists at Afissos; could not confirm which this record is.

name: Παραλία Μπριάνου
evidence: Brianou (Pagania) described as a solitary beach between Agioi Saranta and Banikas, accessible only by boat — no facilities implied.

name: Σουτραλί
evidence: Official bathing-water profile: Soutrali (Agria) is organized with sunbeds, umbrellas, showers and waste bins; restaurants/refreshment bars nearby.

name: Αγία Παρασκευή (Αγιά)
evidence: No source found for this Larissa-coast beach; all 'Agia Paraskevi' results refer to Thesprotia, Evia, Halkidiki etc.

name: Παραλία Στρίντζος
evidence: Results conflated Strintzos with Alexandrini beach near the Pinios estuary (described as organized with beach bars); could not confirm the description applies to this specific beach.
